    Discretised probabilities of a fitted delay

    Source: R/outbreak-delays.R
    epi_delay_pmf.Rd

    Converts a delay distribution from epi_delay_dist() into the probability of each whole-day delay, using the same double interval censoring as the fit, so it can be used as a reporting delay (epi_cfr(), epi_nowcast()) or as generation-interval weights (epi_rt(), after dropping day 0 and renormalising).

    Usage

    epi_delay_pmf(fit, max_delay, family = NULL)

    Arguments

    fit

    A tep_delay tibble from epi_delay_dist().

    max_delay

    Longest delay to include, in days.

    family

    Family to use; defaults to the best by AIC (first row).

    Value

    A tibble with delay (0 to max_delay) and probability, renormalised to sum to one.

    Examples

    set.seed(2)
d <- data.frame(delay = round(rgamma(200, 4, 1)))
fit <- epi_delay_dist(d, delay, family = "gamma")
epi_delay_pmf(fit, max_delay = 15)
#> # A tibble: 16 × 2
#>    delay probability
#>    <int>       <dbl>
#>  1     0    0.00484 
#>  2     1    0.0686  
#>  3     2    0.172   
#>  4     3    0.213   
#>  5     4    0.190   
#>  6     5    0.140   
#>  7     6    0.0913  
#>  8     7    0.0550  
#>  9     8    0.0311  
#> 10     9    0.0168  
#> 11    10    0.00879 
#> 12    11    0.00445 
#> 13    12    0.00220 
#> 14    13    0.00107 
#> 15    14    0.000508
#> 16    15    0.000239
